name: com.orabrain/prax-data-services
title: Prax Data Services
description: Screen banks, wires, sanctions, wallets and transfers before an agent moves money. Free tier.

tools.name: screen_wallet
tools.description: Wallet and smart-contract risk screening (KYT / AML): check any address (EVM chains for full analysis; Bitcoin, Tron, Solana, Litecoin, Monero and other chains against the sanctions lists) against Prax threat intelligence - OFAC and global sanctions, exploits, hacks, phishing, scams, drainers, mixers, malicious contracts, and first-hop exposure to them. Returns risk band, labels, roles, alerts naming it, counterparties and a plain-language story. Use before onboarding, paying or interacting with an address. Free plan. Set live=true for live on-chain screening too.

tools.name: analyze_transaction
tools.description: Transaction risk analysis: given an EVM transaction hash, returns status, value, counterparties and the risk of both sides (sanctions, exploit, phishing, scam exposure) with flags. Use for post-trade monitoring, incident triage and fraud investigation.

tools.name: screen_transfer
tools.description: Pre-signature transfer check (payment screening): is it safe to send `amount` of `asset` from `from` to `to`? Returns allow / review / block with reasons - sanctioned or flagged parties, malicious or scam token, look-alike address poisoning, first-time payee. Works before the transaction exists; no chain lookup needed. Use in wallet, custody, payment and treasury flows.

tools.name: screen_entity
tools.description: Sanctions and export-control screening for people, companies, vessels and crypto addresses: fuzzy name match (aliases, transliterations) or exact wallet / contract lookup against the lists Prax pulls continuously: US OFAC (SDN and Consolidated), UK OFSI, EU, UN and Swiss SECO, every crypto address they list on any chain, plus the US Consolidated Screening List (BIS Entity List, Denied Persons, Unverified and Military End User lists, State nonproliferation and ITAR debarred parties, OFAC sectoral, FSE, CAPTA, menu-based and Chinese military-industrial lists). Returns match / possible_match / no_match with hits (entity, type, programs, list, authority, aliases, addresses, licence requirement, Federal Register notice, score). Use for KYC / KYB onboarding, payment screening and trade compliance. Free plan.

tools.name: screen_wallets_batch
tools.description: Bulk wallet screening: screen_wallet for up to 50 addresses in one call - portfolio, customer-base or deposit-address sweeps. Returns per-address risk band and labels plus a summary.

tools.name: screen_transfers_batch
tools.description: Bulk transfer screening: screen_transfer for up to 50 transfers in one call (items of {from, to, amount, asset, chain}) - payout batches, payroll, exchange withdrawals. Returns a verdict per item and a summary.

tools.name: get_alerts
tools.description: Threat-intelligence alert feed: approved Prax alerts from the last 24 hours (new exploits, attacker wallets, malicious contracts, phishing campaigns, sanctions updates), newest first, same payload as the webhook feed. Use for SOC / compliance monitoring and watchlist updates.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search Prax threat intelligence in plain words (e.g. 'critical attacker wallets on base this week', 'phishing contracts created by 0x...'). Returns COUNTS of matching addresses (by band, chain, role) plus approved alerts from the last 24 h; address lists are not enumerable - look a specific address up with screen_wallet. Filters: chain (eth, base...), risk band (critical, high), role (attacker wallet, malicious contract, deployer, funding ancestry, clone), period (today, last 7 days, since 2026-10-01), free text (bytecode clone, phishing), 'created by 0x...', 'counterparties of 0x...'. An exact address or tx hash returns that record's id. Use fetch(id) for the full record.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch the full Prax intelligence record for an id returned by search (address:<chain>:<addr>, tx:<chain>:<hash>, alert:<id>).

tools.name: screen_bank
tools.description: Counterparty-bank and wire screening: give a BIC (SWIFT), IBAN, US ABA routing number or LEI, and/or a bank name and country, optionally the beneficiary name. Returns allow / review / block with reasons: identifier checksum, the institution from GLEIF (legal name, country, status), jurisdiction lists (FATF call-for-action and increased monitoring, EU high-risk third countries, FinCEN Section 311 jurisdictions, comprehensive US sanctions programmes), the bank on sanctions lists, FinCEN 311 / 9714 institutions, and enforcement actions naming the bank. Use before releasing a wire, onboarding a correspondent or paying a new supplier's bank.

identifier.description: BIC (e.g. DEUTDEFF), IBAN, 9-digit ABA routing number or 20-char LEI

name.description: Bank name (used when the identifier is missing or cannot be resolved)

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the bank, if known

beneficiary_name.description: Beneficiary (payee) name on the wire, screened against sanctions lists

tools.name: screen_enforcement
tools.description: Regulatory enforcement history for a bank, fintech, money services business, crypto firm or individual: consent orders, civil money penalties, fines, final notices, bars and charges from the Federal Reserve, OCC, FDIC, FinCEN, SEC, CFTC and the UK FCA, pulled continuously from the regulators' own releases. Returns match / possible_match / no_match with each action's authority, date, type, title and link. Use in vendor onboarding, correspondent due diligence, KYB and partner reviews.

years.description: Only actions from the last N years (default: all)

tools.name: screen_licence
tools.description: Is this payments or digital-asset firm registered or licensed, where, and is it active: FinCEN MSB registrations (US), NY DFS virtual-currency licensees and trust charters, the EU MiCA register of authorised crypto-asset service providers and the entities national authorities have named as non-compliant (ESMA), Dubai VARA licensed VASPs, Hong Kong SFC licensed virtual asset trading platforms, the UK FCA Financial Services Register (live), plus the firm's LEI record. Returns licensed / flagged / possible_match / not_found with every registration found (authority, number, status, activities, link) and the registries covered, so absence is reported as absence from those registries, not as proof. Use for fintech and VASP onboarding, partner due diligence and crypto-to-bank flows.

jurisdiction.description: Country or region to narrow to (US, US-NY, GB, EU, EU-DE, AE, HK)

tools.name: screen_country
tools.description: Jurisdiction risk for a country (ISO code or name): FATF call-for-action and increased-monitoring lists, EU high-risk third countries, FinCEN Section 311 jurisdictions, OFAC comprehensive sanctions programmes, and how many entries with an address in that country sit on the US export-control and non-SDN lists (BIS Entity, Denied Persons, Unverified and Military End User lists, State nonproliferation and ITAR debarred, OFAC SSI / FSE / CMIC). Returns high / elevated / standard with reasons, the lists and references. Use for country-risk scoring, onboarding, payment corridors and trade compliance.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (DE, VN) or English name (Vietnam)

tools.name: screen_company
tools.description: Does this counterparty exist, who runs it, is it active: legal entity from GLEIF (LEI, status, direct and ultimate parent, subsidiaries), UK Companies House (status, incorporation date, officers, persons with significant control, charges, insolvency, overdue filings; needs the free Companies House key in settings), US SEC EDGAR (CIK, SIC, state, tickers, former names, recent filings), plus the sanctions / export-control lists and enforcement history Prax already screens. Returns allow / review / block with entity_status (active, inactive, not_found, listed) and reasons. Use for KYB, vendor and partner onboarding, invoice and payee verification.

number.description: Company registration number (UK Companies House), if known

jurisdiction.description: GB or US to limit registry lookups (default: both)

tools.name: screen_adverse_media
tools.description: Negative news about a person or company from GDELT (global news index, 15-minute updates): articles that name the counterparty with a financial-crime theme (fraud, money laundering, sanctions, bribery and corruption, enforcement, terrorism financing, cyber, scam, insolvency). Returns adverse / possible / none with each article's title, date, source and link, counts by theme and by source. Use in KYC / KYB onboarding, periodic review and investigations. Prax reports headlines; it does not judge their truth.

tools.name: screen_domain
tools.description: Is this domain, URL or sender domain safe to trust, pay or onboard: malware URL and host lists (URLhaus), hijacked netblocks (Spamhaus DROP), botnet C2 and active-threat IPs behind it, disposable e-mail domains, domain age and registrar from RDAP, MX / SPF / DMARC posture (for an e-mail address: can it receive mail, can it be spoofed), hosting country against the FATF, EU, FinCEN 311 and OFAC lists. Returns allow / review / block with reasons. Use for vendor onboarding, payment-instruction and bank-detail change requests, invoice fraud and phishing triage.

tools.name: screen_ip
tools.description: Is this IP address a known threat: botnet C2 (Feodo Tracker), hijacked / criminal netblocks (Spamhaus DROP), active attackers (CINS), Tor exit nodes, URLhaus hosts, plus the allocation (network, organisation, country from RDAP) and the country against the FATF, EU, FinCEN 311 and OFAC lists. Returns allow / review / block with reasons. Use for login and session risk, instruction-change requests, API callers and SOC triage.

tools.name: screen_securities
tools.description: Can this instrument or issuer be traded, custodied or accepted as collateral: ISIN / CUSIP / SEDOL / ticker resolved through OpenFIGI to the issuer, then the issuer against OFAC NS-CMIC (Chinese military-industrial complex: no purchase or sale of their securities), OFAC sectoral sanctions (new debt / equity restrictions), the sanctions lists, SEC trading suspensions and enforcement history. Returns allow / review / block with reasons and references. Use for pre-trade compliance, onboarding of collateral and tokenised securities, and investment restriction lists.

issuer.description: Issuer name (used when there is no identifier, or to override the resolved name)

tools.name: screen_cve
tools.description: What is this vulnerability and does it matter now: OSV advisory records (summary, severity, affected open-source packages and fixed versions, references) for a CVE, GHSA or OSV id, whether CISA lists it as exploited in the wild (KEV: date added, remediation due date, ransomware use) and its EPSS exploit probability and percentile. Returns exploited / known / unknown with reasons. Use for patch prioritisation, vendor security questionnaires, incident triage and third-party risk reviews.

identifier.description: CVE-2024-3094, GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx or an OSV id (PYSEC-, GO-, RUSTSEC-)

tools.name: screen_package
tools.description: Known vulnerabilities in an open-source package at a given version (software supply chain): PyPI, npm, Go, Maven, crates.io, NuGet, RubyGems, Packagist, Pub, Hex, Debian, Alpine and more, from OSV (live API plus Prax's local copy), each advisory with severity, whether it is exploited in the wild (CISA KEV), EPSS, and the fixed version. Returns allow / review / block with reasons. Use for dependency reviews, SBOM checks, vendor stack assessments and change approvals.

ecosystem.description: PyPI, npm, Go, Maven, crates.io, NuGet, RubyGems, Packagist, Pub, Hex, Debian, Alpine, Ubuntu, Linux, GitHub Actions

name.description: Package name (Maven: group:artifact; Go: module path)

version.description: Installed version; omit to list every advisory for the package

tools.name: screen_packages
tools.description: Up to 50 packages in one call ({ecosystem, name, version} each), for an SBOM or a lock file: per-package verdict, advisories, fixed versions, and a summary (block / review / allow counts). Same sources as screen_package.
